key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings favor long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces their friction coefficient and wear rate.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameter control can help produce protective coatings for carbon steel, with wear performance evaluated under service-relevant humidity.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Assess droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and corrosion behavior.
Test friction and wear against Si3N4 balls under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear results involve Si3N4 counterfaces; transferability to other contact materials requires validation.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
